stops.segment: Papers Found After His Decease
stops.stop: Paris, the fire and salt printed at last
stops.date_confidence: contested and left contested. English Wikipedia's works list says first edition 1608 but gives the catalogued imprint as Paris, Abel Langelier, 1618; musicologie.org lists only Paris, Vve A. L'Angelier, 1618. Abel L'Angelier died in 1610, so an 1618 Paris printing is by his widow, and the 1608/1618 split is two imprints rather than a typographical error. Only 1618 is bibliographically attested in the sources reached, so it is used here.
